scope: Proposition A.1 (Finite shooting bounds) of the manuscript “A finite-time singularity of Calabi flow on projective space” (preprints/A-finite-time-singularity-of-Calabi-flow-on-projective-space-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 352 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 486e9e5ff47e92a4), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 41. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every parameter z∗ ∈ [−R, R]2, where R = 5·10−10, let (k, d) be given by (3.6), and let p be the origin solution of (3.5) supplied by Lemma 3.2. This solution extends to 0 ≤ s ≤ S0 = 56 and satisfies 1 + p(s) > 0. For the coordinates of its jet relative to pa, defined in (3.12), one has |q| ≤ .25R, (ℜξ, ℑξ) − z∗ ∞ ≤ .13R. (A.1)
